title: SLO-aware fanout budget and progressive backoff framework
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Services in high-concurrency paths are causing cascading failures during regional outages and traffic spikes because callers fan out to many replicas or failover regions without any coordinated budget. Current retry and backoff behavior is inconsistent across services and SDKs: some clients perform aggressive hedging, others retry with fixed intervals, and idempotency metadata is spotty. This ticket designs and implements a SLO-driven fanout budget and progressive backoff framework that standardizes behavior across services and client SDKs, integrates with regional failover policies, and preserves correctness via idempotency tokens. Goals: 1) Define a lightweight 'fanout budget' model that caps concurrent hedged requests per logical operation based on SLO class and current regional capacity; 2) Provide a progressive backoff strategy that de-escalates fanout and increases token use during degradation; 3) Formalize idempotency token header semantics for retriable and hedged calls; 4) Add runtime hooks to the gateway and SDKs to enforce budgets and emit telemetry used by SLO controllers; 5) Ship server and SDK changes with a migration path and automated compatibility checks. Non-goals: redesigning global routing, changing existing SLO definitions, or removing all service-specific retry knobs.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative fanout budget spec is published and reviewed in Confluence
Gateway and runtime enforce per-operation fanout budget with telemetry exposed to Console
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) implement a common backoff/hedging library and honor idempotency header semantics
Integration test suite validates correctness: no duplicate side-effecting operations when idempotency header present
E2E canary in two services shows reduced p99 tail latency and fewer cross-region overload incidents during a simulated region pause
Monitoring: new SLO-oriented dashboards (per-operation fanout, hedged-rate, idempotency-failures) are available in Console release-1.20
tasks: Design fanout budget model and mapping from SLO classes to budget caps (PM + SRE)
Draft idempotency header schema and update API compatibility guide
Implement middleware in gateway/runtime to cap hedged requests and emit hedging telemetry
Extract SDK retry/backoff primitives into a shared library and add hedging option with budget signals
Add integration tests that inject failures and verify single-commit semantics for write APIs
Create migration playbook for teams to opt-in and roll out canary by operation
Dashboarding: add queries for fanout budget utilization, hedged vs primary success rate, duplicate-detection rate
Run 2-week canary on payments-service and embeddings-ingest with gradual ramping
progress_updates: 2026-01-18: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, SDK and PM. Agreed SLO classes: Gold/Silver/Bronze. Decided budget will be expressed as max concurrent outbound hedges per request type.
2026-01-25: Draft spec uploaded to Confluence (see links). Received initial design feedback from Lina Zhou: prefer soft-deny over hard-fail for legacy callers.

2026-01-30: Runtime prototype implemented: gateway exposes /v1/hedge-token endpoint and enforces per-operation budget in in-memory controller. Local perf tests show budget enforcement adds ~1.2% CPU overhead.
2026-02-04: SDK alpha for JS and Go created with shared backoff primitives; python wrapper pending. PRs: GH#redwood/runtime PR 1429, GH#redwood/sdk-js PR 557.
2026-02-09: Integration test added to ci/hedging-suite that simulates regional pause; initial run indicates duplicate write rate <0.01% when idempotency header present.
2026-02-10: PM review sign-off on spec with two requested changes: clearer migration steps and explicit metric names. Work moving to canary preparation.
2026-02-24: (planned) Start canary ramping on payments-service (step 1: 5% traffic)
decisions: Prefer per-operation soft-deny: when budget is exhausted, SDKs will fallback to single-attempt with exponential backoff rather than immediate error; gateway returns budget-metrics header so callers can adapt.
Idempotency token naming: use header 'Idempotency-Key' with 64-byte limit and include algorithm version 'v1' prefix for future upgrades.
Hedging window default: max 2 hedged attempts within 100ms for Gold SLO, 1 within 200ms for Silver, no hedging for Bronze unless explicitly enabled.
Telemetry: emit hedging_attempt, hedging_success, hedging_duplicate_detected, fanout_budget_utilization tags (operation, region, slo_class).
Migration: start with read-heavy operations and non-critical writes in canaries; require manual opt-in for stateful write endpoints until integration tests pass.
implementation_notes: Key trade-offs considered: 1) central vs local budget controllers — chose hybrid: local memory controller with periodic sync to central policy to avoid control-plane latency; 2) strict idempotency enforcement at gateway vs application layer — we rely on app-level duplicate detection for legacy endpoints but require idempotency header for hedging to guarantee single-commit semantics. SDKs will add helper to generate and cache Idempotency-Key per logical operation.
postmortem_plan: If canary shows increased duplicate commits >0.1% or unexpected latency regressions, pause rollout, collect trace samples with hedging headers, and run targeted replay tests. Run incident retro and feed fixes into next patch (runtime-1.20.1).
notes: Owner to coordinate with platform-security before enabling hedging for Private/VPC deployments due to auditability concerns. Expect follow-up tickets to add RBAC toggles and HSM-backed idempotency-key rotation if required.
